project: Quran Forced Alignment - Model B Failure Analysis

failures.likely_cause: The melismatic elongation on the syllable 'بَٰ' (normalized as 'با') was held for 1.84 seconds. Since the model lacks a continuous vocalic representation for extreme durations, CTC emissions decayed into blank tokens. The Viterbi solver shifted to 'ر' and 'ك' too early, resulting in a premature word boundary assignment.
failures.evidence_frames: Frames 11 to 107 are aligned to 'ا', but the model confidence scores drops to under 0.15 past frame 45, leading to alignment drift.

failures.likely_cause: The Tanween on 'شَىْءٍ' is assimilated into the 'ق' of 'قَدِيرٌ' (resulting in a nasal Ghunnah). No distinct 'ن' (Nun) is produced acoustically. Because Model B uses standard Arabic letters without phonetic representation of nasalization, the trellis maps 'ن' across low-probability frames, pushing the end of 'شَىْءٍ' into the beginning of 'قَدِيرٌ'.
failures.evidence_frames: Frames 223 to 256 are mapped to 'ش', 'ى', 'ء' but the boundary between 'شَىْءٍ' and 'قَدِيرٌ' is blurred by a 240ms transition zone.
